name: Capacity Crisis
from: Idea two (data center executive), refined: a management sim around Jevons’ paradox. Working title.
hook: You cut the cost of a query in half. Your customers order three times as many.
pitch: You own a data center, and every efficiency upgrade makes it cheaper for customers to use. In this management sim built around Jevons’ paradox, a better chip can ease the strain on your power supply in the morning and leave you scrambling to keep the lights on by afternoon. The big decision is what to do with the capacity you free up: sell it, save it for the next rush, or set a limit while you still can.
minute_check: Yes, if the first upgrade visibly backfires within a minute of play.
build_check: Yes: one map, three upgrades, one demand curve.
scope: Seven days, three upgrades. The demand curve is the opponent; tune it first.

brief.player: The owner of a data center.
brief.goal: Get through a week of days without a blackout while staying profitable.
brief.fail: Demand outruns power: a blackout ends the run.
brief.ending: Week’s end: how much you sold, saved or capped, and what happened to the town’s power.
brief.verb: Allocate: sell, save or cap the capacity each upgrade frees.
brief.theme: Jevons’ paradox: making something more efficient makes people use more of it.
brief.look: A town map whose lights flicker as load rises; a plain dashboard beside it.

prov.bug: New chip! Half the power per query!
prov.nit: Then why did the power bill go up by lunch?

refs_lit: William Stanley Jevons, The Coal Question (1865)
Where the paradox comes from: more efficient steam engines made Britain burn more coal, not less.
A city that answers your building with demand; a tested way to show load on a map.
A single heat source the whole city depends on, and choices about who gets it.
omni_gameplay_prompt: Clean isometric-top-down infrastructure management game on dark slate (#0f1418) with cool white (#e8eef2) town blocks and warm amber (#f2b84b) power lines. Steady angled overhead camera over a miniature town beside a server farm. As gleaming new chip modules snap into the data center halls, glowing amber electricity surges triple in speed along the cables, causing peaceful neighborhood house windows to flicker and dim toward blackout while cooling towers vent plumes of steam. Continuous unbroken gameplay shot, no scene cuts, no gibberish text. Use the reference image for map-and-meter composition. Sound design: transformer hum rising in pitch, relay switches clicking. No dialogue.
